- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or volatile, model often overestimates near-term upside — cap upward slope or reduce early forecast increments.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots — apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to recognize — adjust forecast downward with smoother decay curve.  
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is rising, model underestimates momentum — increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early peaks — apply “lag correction”: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast at 10–15 day mark if sentiment is neutral or declining.
